title: The subfield with $q^n$ elements of an algebraic closure of $\mathbf F_q$

source.place: node def-weil-finite-field-fiber, order 411: 'For every integer $n\geq1$, let $\mathbf F_{q^n}\subset k$ be the unique subfield with $q^n$ elements' (existence and uniqueness asserted without argument; the $k_0$-algebra structure of $\mathbf F_{q^n}$, needed for $\operatorname{Hom}_{k_0}(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_{q^n},Y_0)$, is not mentioned). No document in literature/ proves it: Stacks Tag 09HY (Fields, Section 9.14) only shows that a finite field has $p^f$ elements and a cyclic unit group; the standard reference is Lang, Algebra, Ch. V, §5, Theorem 5.1 (not obtained)

proof.text: Setup. $k_0$ has characteristic $p$ and $q$ elements [def-weil-finite-field-q-elements]; the ring homomorphism $\iota:k_0\to k$ is injective since $k_0$ is a field [def-pc-field-extension], and $p\cdot1_k=\iota(p\cdot1_{k_0})=0$, so $k$ has characteristic $p$. Fix $n\geq1$ and put $Q=q^n=p^{an}$; then $p\mid Q$ and $Q\geq2$.

source.place: Lang, Algebra, Ch. V, §5, Theorem 5.1 (wanted, not obtained); proof written by an agent along the lines of that theorem

proof.text: Clause 1, subfield. By [def-weil-frobenius-substitution] the map $\varphi_q:z\mapsto z^q$ is a field automorphism of $k$ fixing $\iota(k_0)$ pointwise, hence so is its $n$-th iterate $\varphi_q^n:z\mapsto z^{q^n}$. The set $k^{(n)}=\{x\in k:\varphi_q^n(x)=x\}$ is the fixed set of a field automorphism, hence a subfield of $k$: it contains $0,1$, and if $\varphi_q^n(x)=x$ and $\varphi_q^n(y)=y$ then $\varphi_q^n(x\pm y)=x\pm y$, $\varphi_q^n(xy)=xy$ and, for $x\neq0$, $\varphi_q^n(x^{-1})=\varphi_q^n(x)^{-1}=x^{-1}$. It contains $\iota(k_0)$ because $\varphi_q$ fixes $\iota(k_0)$ pointwise. By definition $k^{(n)}$ is the set of roots in $k$ of $f_n=X^{q^n}-X$ [def-weil-polynomial-root].

source.place: Lang, Algebra, Ch. V, §5, Theorem 5.1 (wanted, not obtained); proof written by an agent along the lines of that theorem

proof.text: Clause 1, cardinality. The polynomial $f_n=X^{Q}-X\in k[X]$ is monic of degree $Q$ (as $Q\geq2>1$), and $k$ is algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], so by [lem-weil-alg-closed-linear-factorization] $f_n=\prod_{j=1}^{Q}(X-\gamma_j)$ with $\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_Q\in k$ (the number of factors equals the degree, the leading coefficient is $1$). An element $x\in k$ is a root of $f_n$ iff $x=\gamma_j$ for some $j$ ($k$ is a field, so a product vanishes iff a factor does). Since $k$ has characteristic $p$ and $p\mid Q$, every root of $f_n$ is simple [lem-weil-frobenius-polynomial-simple-roots], so the $\gamma_j$ are pairwise distinct (if $\gamma_i=\gamma_j$ with $i\neq j$, then $(X-\gamma_i)^2\mid f_n$). Hence $k^{(n)}=\{\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_Q\}$ has exactly $Q=q^n$ elements.

source.place: Lang, Algebra, Ch. V, §5, Theorem 5.1 (wanted, not obtained); proof written by an agent along the lines of that theorem

proof.text: Clause 2, uniqueness. Let $E\subseteq k$ be a subfield with $q^n$ elements. By [lem-weil-finite-field-pow-card] applied to $E$ (a finite field with $Q=q^n$ elements), $x^{q^n}=x$ for every $x\in E$, so $E\subseteq k^{(n)}$. Both are finite sets with $q^n$ elements (step 3), so $E=k^{(n)}$.

source.place: Section 9.14 'Finite fields' (Tag 09HY) for the unit group of order $q^n-1$ behind [lem-weil-finite-field-pow-card]; the containment-and-counting argument is Lang, Algebra, Ch. V, §5, Theorem 5.1 (wanted), written by an agent

proof.text: Clause 3. $\iota(k_0)$ is a subfield of $k$ (the image of a field under a ring homomorphism) with $q$ elements ($\iota$ is injective, step 1). By step 4 with $n=1$, $\iota(k_0)=k^{(1)}$, and it is the only subfield of $k$ with $q$ elements. Moreover $k^{(1)}\subseteq k^{(n)}$: if $x^q=x$ then by induction on $m$, $x^{q^{m}}=(x^{q^{m-1}})^q=x^q=x$; in particular $\iota(k_0)\subseteq k^{(n)}$ (as also seen in step 2).

source.place: Lang, Algebra, Ch. V, §5, Theorem 5.1 (wanted, not obtained); proof written by an agent along the lines of that theorem

proof.text: Consequence. By clauses 1 and 2, '$\mathbf F_{q^n}$, the unique subfield of $k$ with $q^n$ elements' names the well-defined subfield $k^{(n)}$. By clause 3, $\iota$ takes values in $k^{(n)}$, so its corestriction $\iota_n:k_0\to k^{(n)}$ is a ring homomorphism and makes $\mathbf F_{q^n}=k^{(n)}$ a field extension of $k_0$, i.e. a $k_0$-algebra [def-pc-field-extension], with $\iota$ equal to the composite of $\iota_n$ and the inclusion $k^{(n)}\subseteq k$.

Wrote a six-step agent proof along Lang, Algebra V §5 Thm 5.1 (wanted, already in literature/LIST.md): the roots of X^{q^n}-X are the fixed points of the n-th power of the Frobenius substitution, hence a subfield containing iota(k_0); they number q^n because X^{q^n}-X splits in the algebraically closed k (lem-weil-alg-closed-linear-factorization) with simple roots (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-frobenius-polynomial-simple-roots); a subfield with q^n elements lies inside by x^{q^n}=x (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-finite-field-pow-card, whose input is Stacks 09HY) and equals it by counting; clause 3 is the case n=1. Statement kept; stmt_deps gain def-weil-polynomial-root and def-pc-field-extension (roots, k_0-algebra structure). No Mathlib lemma states the whole result; search recorded.
